sketches.title: Haunting House Call
sketches.premise: Two ghost hunters send ordinary hauntings into a house, one at a time. Each new haunting must deal with the haunting already there, until one haunting cannot handle its job.
sketches.criterion: A move wins when its haunting plausibly blocks, drives out, traps, exposes, or otherwise defeats the standing haunting; hiding, merely surviving, and using a stronger copy of the same haunting lose.
sketches.move_shape: Name one standing haunting and say what it does to the haunting before it: "I am a ringing phone; I call the ghost out of the walls."
sketches.first_card: A cold spot in the hallway

sketches.title: Ghost Trap Trial
sketches.premise: A ghost is on trial, and each player adds one piece of evidence about what kind of haunting it is. Your evidence must explain away, expose, or trap the evidence already on the table.
sketches.criterion: The judge accepts a move only if the new clue directly defeats the old clue by revealing its cause, proving it false, or making it useless; dodging the clue, outlasting it, or repeating it louder loses.
sketches.move_shape: Give one plain clue and its effect on the clue before it: "I am muddy footprints; I show the invisible ghost is not flying."

sketches.title: Haunted House Rules
sketches.premise: Players take turns writing rules for a haunted house, but every new rule must shut down the rule before it. The house grows stranger until someone writes a rule that cannot control what stands.
sketches.criterion: A rule beats the standing rule when it clearly limits, cancels, reverses, or exploits it; ignoring the rule, merely enduring it, and making the same rule more extreme do not count.
sketches.move_shape: State one house rule and how it defeats the previous one: "No one may speak after midnight; this stops the rule that summons a ghost when you say its name."

sketches.title: Spirit Switchboard
sketches.premise: Two players operate a haunted telephone exchange. Each call connects one ghostly caller to the previous caller, and the new caller must interrupt, redirect, silence, or outwit that connection.
sketches.criterion: A caller overcomes the standing caller by plausibly cutting off, confusing, rerouting, revealing, or taking control of its call; refusing to answer, waiting it out, and adding a louder version of the same call lose.
sketches.move_shape: Name a caller and the call it makes: "I am a wrong number; I send the ghost's warning to an empty house."
sketches.first_card: A child whispers from the receiver

sketches.title: Ghost Story Court
sketches.premise: Players tell a haunting one sentence at a time, but each sentence must make the previous sentence’s spooky claim harmless, impossible, or useful to the living. The first sentence that cannot do so ends the story.
sketches.criterion: A sentence beats the standing sentence when its plain meaning logically undercuts, explains, contains, or turns the earlier haunting against itself; a mere escape, survival, or bigger scare is a loss.
sketches.move_shape: Add one sentence and explain the turn: "The ghost appeared in the mirror, but the mirror was facing the ghost, so it saw only itself."
sketches.first_card: At midnight, the dead man knocked three times

sketches.title: Haunting Cleanup
sketches.premise: A messy haunting leaves one problem behind at a time, and players send in a tool, person, or small act to solve it. Each solution must deal with the exact spooky nuisance already present, not simply avoid it.
sketches.criterion: The new solution wins when it plausibly removes, calms, seals, exposes, or repurposes the standing nuisance; hiding from it, being too tough to notice it, and using a larger version of its own force lose.
sketches.move_shape: Name one practical solution and its action: "I am a box of salt; I make a line the wandering ghost cannot cross."
sketches.first_card: A wet footprint appears on the ceiling
